newsitem.title: USA: Archer plan includes tax-exempt bond provisions.
newsitem.headline: Archer plan includes tax-exempt bond provisions.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer on Monday proposed increasing the amount of tax-exempt bonds that may be issued for schools and charitable groups.
The provision is part of an $85 billion tax relief plan proposed by the Texas Republican at a packed news conference.
The Archer plan includes several arbitrage rebate provisions. It would repeal the $100,000 limit on unspent proceeds from tax-exempt bond issues under certain rebate exceptions.

The bill would include an exclusion from arbitrage rebate for earnings on bona fide debt service funds under bond rules involving construction. It would repeal a debt service-based limitation on investment in certain "non-purpose" purchases.
The bill also would repeal expired student loan bond arbitrage rebate provisions.

The proposal also includes an education tax provision of interest to the municipal bond market. It would raise the $150 million volume cap on so-called 501(c)(3) bonds, other than hospital bonds, by $10 million annually until it reaches $200 million.
